title: Cross-team Roadmap Dependency Hub and OKR Alignment
creator: Leah Martinez
description:
Problem: Roadmap-level dependencies across Eng, Design, Security and Infra often surface late (sprint N) and cause schedule slippage. Current visibility is scattered: Linear tickets for individual teams, ad-hoc spreadsheets, and periodic syncs. Goal: build a lightweight, single-pane Roadmap Dependency Hub that surfaces explicit upstream/downstream links, OKR alignment, and blocking risk so PMs and ICs can remediate early.

Scope: (1) Data model and sync layer to ingest dependency links from Linear + GitHub + Figma annotations; (2) Console UI panel showing timeline swimlanes, dependency graph overlay, and per-dependency metadata (owner, type, ETA, mitigation plan); (3) Alerts and weekly digest for high-risk blockers; (4) OKR mapping per initiative and cycle-level rollups.

Out-of-scope for MVP: full two-way edit from Console back into Linear (read-only sync for MVP); automated resourcing suggestions.

Why now: We have recurring misses on Dedicated and Private launches tied to infra/security handoffs. This reduces rework and helps sales-sensitive timelines by making cross-team commitments explicit.
acceptance_criteria: Hub shows all dependencies for initiatives tagged 'RoadmapVisibility' with linkable rows to source Linear issues
Dependency type and owner are editable in Console (MVP: edit only for PMs via ad-hoc metadata, later via two-way sync)
OKR field maps to initiatives and aggregates coverage per cycle (example view: 2026-W10 shows % initiatives with OKR mapping)
High-risk blockers (customer_impact=high OR due_date within 7 days and unresolved) raise an alert in Console and send a Slack digest to #pm-ops and #eng-oncall
Security and infra dependencies are flagged and require a security_review_required tag before release acceptance
comments: 2026-03-02 - Leah Martinez: Created ticket after weekly GTM retrospective; attached examples of missed dependencies from runtime-1.18 and private-deploy blackouts. Marking as cross-team priority.

2026-03-04 - Arjun Patel: Drafted PRD and proposed two implementation options: A) Build as Console-integrated panel (single codepath) or B) Build separate service with UI and embed. Leaning A for faster shipping; trade-off is more Console surface area management. Linked PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/roadmap-deps/prd-2026-03

2026-03-05 - Design review (Maya Chen): Shared low-fidelity flows in Figma for swimlane + graph overlay. Concern: screen real-estate for enterprise orgs with many teams. Proposed collapsing groups and collapsible lanes: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz/roadmap-deps

2026-03-06 - ENG sync (Sasha Kim): Agreed on data model: dependency object = {source_issue, target_issue, relation_type, owner, status, mitigation}. Implementation will use a read-only Linear webhook + nightly GitHub PR scan to infer cross-references. Engineering estimate: 8 pts for MVP backend + 5 pts for UI. Plan: deliver backend by 2026-03-28, UI by 2026-04-08.

2026-03-08 - Security (Omar Ruiz): Flagged requirements for storing issue links and notes; must ensure PII/secret-sources are not persisted. Security review requested. Added security checklist link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/security/roadmap-deps-checklist

2026-03-10 - Arjun Patel: Spike completed for Linear webhook ingestion; prototype stores dependency metadata in protected Console namespace. Found one blocker: Linear API pagination on large workspaces; will batch-sync and add a cursor. Github PR for ingestion spike: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1287

2026-03-12 - Leah Martinez: PM review — requested explicit UX for 'mitigation plan' and escalation path. Also requested OKR tag auto-suggest based on initiative title heuristics. Added to backlog for a follow-up story.
2026-03-13 - Design (Maya Chen): Submitted updated mocks with collapsible lanes and filter-by-dependency-type. Attached figma and short usability notes. Ready for implementation handoff.
notes_summary: MVP will be read-only sync into Console; prioritized visibility and alerting. Trade-off: no immediate two-way edit; benefit: faster ship and lower risk surface for migration.
outcome_metrics: Reduce cross-team blocking time by 30% for tagged initiatives within first quarter after launch
Surface >=90% of roadmap dependencies in Console for teams using 'RoadmapVisibility' tagging
Increase OKR-mapped initiatives coverage to 95% per cycle
